summary: Remote-controlled agent daemon executes commands from a hardcoded gateway WebSocket
details: The npm package installs a `whalent` bin that starts a daemon (dist/index.cjs) which opens a WebSocket connection to a configurable gateway (default `wss://your-server/gw/sdk/ws`) and executes commands received from that gateway on the installer's host. Per the shipped README, the daemon 'accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) via the gateway.' Bundled dependencies and strings indicate the remote-control surface extends beyond self-upgrade to interactive shell / terminal forwarding: `ws`, `ssh2`, `@xterm/headless`, and optional `node-pty` are declared; the bundle references `process.env.SHELL` and loopback ports `127.0.0.1:3389`, `127.0.0.1:5900`, `127.0.0.1:5901` (RDP/VNC). The main bundles `dist/index.cjs` (110 KB) and `dist/core.cjs` (13.3 MB) are heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (string-array rotation, hex identifiers, control-flow flattening), concealing the exact dispatch logic. Whoever operates or compromises the gateway can drive PTY/shell execution on any host running this daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
